newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares rise on speculation.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares rise on speculation.

text.p: Nigerian shares climbed higher in speculation-driven trade on Thursday, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 6222.18, up from 6181.99 on Wednesday.
"The market has been very bullish this week based on speculation," one dealer said. "There is no new information in the market responsible for this."
West African Portland Cement rose 70 kobo to 29.10 naira. Dealers said its low price/earnings ratio was responsible for the jump.
Newly-listed Guaranty Trust Bank gained 48 kobo to 11.60 naira, with investors still clamoring for its shares.
PZ Industries, a leading conglomerate, rose 30 kobo to 33.60 naira. Construction firm G. Cappa rose 28 kobo to 5.80 naira.
Oil shares were also on the advance, led by Unipetrol's 30 kobo rise to 35.15 naira. National Oil gained 28 kobo to 28.10 naira.
Active trading in food shares saw Flour Mills move up 20 kobo to 9.40 naira, while Nigerian Bottling Co gained 10 kobo to 26.60 naira.
French conglomerate CFAO led the few losers, sliding 20 kobo to 5.20 naira because of recent poor performance.
An abundance of Guinness shares on offer depressed the price of the brewery by five kobo to 9.50 naira.
CMB and First Aluminium lost five kobo to 4.40 naira and 5.30 naira, respectively.
